paper_identity.title: Critical behavior in the variation of GDR width at low temperature

cross_mass_significance: Establishes the fundamental cross-mass contrast in GDR damping: in open-shell transitional nuclei (119Sb, 120Sn), softness in the free energy surface allows thermal shape fluctuations (TSFM) to expand the GDR width from 4.8 to 11.5 MeV as T increases to 2.0 MeV, whereas in doubly-magic 208Pb the giant shell gap locks spherical stiffness and suppresses thermal broadening, proving that universal temperature-dependent GDR width formulas cannot be transferred between magic and open-shell nuclei.
